frs_sections.title: ABSTRACT
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

This specification defines a low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) built from two
layers: the LoRa physical layer (PHY), a proprietary Semtech Chirp Spread
Spectrum (CSS) modulation operating in the sub-GHz ISM bands, and the LoRaWAN
medium-access-control (MAC) layer standardized by the LoRa Alliance. LoRa CSS
trades data rate for link budget: by spreading a low-rate payload across a wide
RF chirp it achieves very high receiver sensitivity (down to about -148 dBm) and
long range (several to >15 km) at milliwatt transmit power, enabling battery
lifetimes measured in years. LoRaWAN organizes end-devices, gateways, and a
network server into a star-of-stars topology, defines device Classes A/B/C,
over-the-air (OTAA…

frs_sections.title: Bandwidth
frs_sections.content:
-------------
LoRa channels use a bandwidth (BW) of 125 kHz, 250 kHz, or 500 kHz. Most
sub-GHz LoRaWAN uplink channels use 125 kHz. A wider bandwidth gives a higher
data rate (shorter symbol time) but a lower link budget. The symbol rate is
Rsym = BW / 2^SF symbols per second; the chip rate equals the bandwidth (Rc =
BW chips/s).

3.4 Coding Rate (Forward Error Correction)
------------------------------------------
LoRa applies a cyclic forward-error-correction (FEC) code with a coding rate
(CR) of 4/5, 4/6, 4/7, or 4/8. A coding rate of 4/5 adds one parity bit per
four data bits (lowest overhead); 4/8 adds four parity bits per four data bits
(strongest protection, highest overhead). The effective bit rate is
Rb = SF * (BW / 2^SF) * CR.

frs_sections.title: RF Bands and Link Budget
frs_sections.content:
----------------------------
LoRa operates in the license-free sub-GHz ISM bands. Regional plans include
EU868 (863-870 MHz) and US915 (902-928 MHz), among others (AS923, AU915,
IN865, KR920, CN470). The combination of CSS processing gain, narrow bandwidth,
and high coding rate yields a link budget of about 154 dB and receiver
sensitivity to roughly -148 dBm at SF12/125 kHz, supporting ranges of several
kilometers in urban areas and >15 km in line-of-sight rural deployments.

frs_sections.title: Device Classes A / B / C
frs_sections.content:
----------------------------
Every LoRaWAN end-device implements Class A; Class B and Class C are optional
extensions that change the downlink-reception behavior:
  - Class A (mandatory, lowest power): each uplink is followed by exactly two
    short downlink receive windows (RX1, RX2). The server can only send a
    downlink during those windows. The device sleeps the rest of the time.
    Bidirectional, end-device-initiated, lowest power consumption.
  - Class B (beacon, scheduled): in addition to Class A windows, the device
    opens scheduled "ping slot" receive windows synchronized to a periodic
    gateway beacon, allowing the server to initiate downlinks with bounded
    latency. Requires a time-synchronizing beacon.
  - Class C (continuous): the device keeps its receiver open conti…

frs_sections.title: CHANNEL ACCESS
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

5.1 ALOHA + Duty Cycle
----------------------
LoRaWAN end-devices use unslotted ALOHA: a device transmits whenever it has
data, with no listen-before-talk in most regions. To bound interference, the
regional parameters impose a duty cycle limit (e.g. 1% per sub-band in EU868),
restricting the fraction of time a device may occupy a channel. Some regions use
listen-before-talk (LBT) and/or dwell-time limits instead.

frs_sections.title: Receive Windows RX1 and RX2
frs_sections.content:
-------------------------------
After every Class A uplink the device opens two receive windows:
  - RX1 opens RECEIVE_DELAY1 (default 1 s) after the end of the uplink, on the
    same channel and (by default) the same data rate as the uplink (offset by
    RX1DROffset).
  - RX2 opens RECEIVE_DELAY2 (default 2 s) after the uplink on a fixed,
    region-specific frequency and data rate (e.g. 869.525 MHz / DR0 in EU868).
If the device receives a valid downlink preamble in RX1 it does not open RX2.

5.3 Adaptive Data Rate (ADR)
----------------------------
Adaptive Data Rate lets the network optimize each device's spreading factor and
transmit power. When a device sets the ADR bit, the network server observes the

frs_sections.title: MAC COMMANDS
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

MAC commands manage the link between the end-device and the network server. They
are carried in the FOpts field (piggybacked) or in an FPort 0 frame. Each command
has a request (from the server) and an answer (from the device), or vice versa:
  - LinkCheckReq / LinkCheckAns      : device asks for link margin / gateway count.
  - LinkADRReq / LinkADRAns          : server sets data rate, TX power, channel mask.
  - DutyCycleReq / DutyCycleAns      : server sets the device's max duty cycle.
  - RXParamSetupReq / RXParamSetupAns: server sets RX1DROffset, RX2 DR, RX2 freq.
  - DevStatusReq / DevStatusAns      : server asks for battery level and margin.
  - NewChannelReq / NewChannelAns    : server defines/modifies…

frs_sections.title: Reset / power-on
frs_sections.content:
--------------------
On power-up an OTAA device enters JOIN and must complete the join procedure
before sending data. An ABP device already holds DevAddr/NwkSKey/AppSKey and may
transmit immediately, restoring its frame counters from non-volatile memory.

frs_sections.title: TEST / DEBUG / COMPLIANCE
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

Conformance is established by the LoRa Alliance Certification program against
the LoRaWAN L2 specification and the Regional Parameters. Observability includes:
  - DevStatusReq/Ans (battery level, demodulation margin).
  - LinkCheckReq/Ans (link margin, gateway count).
  - Frame-counter and MIC-failure counters.
  - RSSI and SNR of received frames (reported by the gateway/network server).
The LoRaWAN certification test harness exercises join, ADR, the MAC commands,
the receive-window timing, and the class behaviors.

================================================================================

The LoRa PHY (CSS modulation) is a stable Semtech proprietary layer; the LoRaWAN
MAC is an open LoRa Alliance standard layered on top of it.

protocol_overview.type: Low-power wide-area network (LPWAN). Two layers: the Semtech LoRa PHY (Chirp Spread Spectrum, SF7-SF12, 125/250/500 kHz, coding rate 4/5..4/8) and the LoRa Alliance LoRaWAN MAC (star-of-stars, Classes A/B/C, OTAA/ABP, ADR, duty cycle, RX1/RX2, MAC commands, FCnt, MIC).
protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex, end-device-initiated. Class A: each uplink is followed by two short downlink windows (RX1/RX2). Class B adds scheduled ping slots; Class C keeps the receiver open continuously.
protocol_overview.modulation: Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS): each symbol is a linear frequency chirp across the channel bandwidth, encoding SF bits by its cyclic start frequency; up-chirp / down-chirp.
protocol_overview.channel_access: unslotted ALOHA with regional duty-cycle limits
protocol_overview.security: AES-128: 4-byte MIC (AES-128-CMAC, NwkSKey) + payload encryption (AES-128-CTR, AppSKey); FCnt replay protection.
layers: Application layer (application payload, AppSKey end-to-end encryption)
LoRaWAN MAC layer (Classes A/B/C, OTAA/ABP, ADR, MAC commands, FCnt/MIC, RX windows, duty cycle)
LoRa PHY layer (CSS modulation, SF/BW/CR, preamble+sync+header+payload+CRC frame, sub-GHz RF)

compliance_requirements: CSS modulation with SF7-SF12 and 125/250/500 kHz bandwidth.
Coding rate 4/5..4/8 FEC; preamble + sync word + payload + CRC frame.
Class A mandatory; RX1/RX2 windows at the regional delays.
OTAA and/or ABP activation with the LoRaWAN key hierarchy.
ADR support and the standard MAC-command set.
AES-128 MIC (4 bytes) + payload encryption; FCnt replay protection.
LoRa Alliance certification against LoRaWAN L2 + Regional Parameters.

auto_cited_sections.heading: Frame Structure: Preamble + Sync Word + Header + Payload + CRC

functional_requirements.text: The PHY shall use Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS): each symbol is a linear chirp over the channel bandwidth carrying SF bits (2^SF chips/symbol).
The Spreading Factor shall be one of SF7..SF12; symbol duration Tsym = 2^SF / BW. Higher SF gives more range/sensitivity and lower data rate.
The channel bandwidth shall be 125, 250, or 500 kHz; the chip rate equals the bandwidth and the symbol rate is BW / 2^SF.
A forward-error-correction coding rate of 4/5, 4/6, 4/7, or 4/8 shall be applied.

A PHY frame shall consist of a preamble (default 8 up-chirps), a sync word (0x34 public / 0x12 private), an optional explicit header (length, CR, header CRC), the payload, and a 16-bit payload CRC on uplinks.
LoRaWAN shall use a star-of-stars: each uplink is received by all in-range gateways and forwarded to a central network server; gateways are transparent bridges.
Every end-device shall implement Class A (two RX windows after each uplink); Class B (beacon ping slots) and Class C (continuous receive) are optional extensions.
A device shall be activated by OTAA (Join-Request with DevEUI/JoinEUI/DevNonce -> Join-Accept; derive DevAddr, NwkSKey, AppSKey from AppKey) or ABP (pre-provisioned DevAddr/NwkSKey/AppSKey).
When the ADR bit is set, the network server may issue LinkADRReq to set the device's data rate (SF), TX power, and channel mask; the device answers with LinkADRAns.
After a Class A uplink the device shall open RX1 at RECEIVE_DELAY1 (default 1 s, same channel/DR offset) and, if no RX1 downlink, RX2 at RECEIVE_DELAY2 (default 2 s, fixed region freq/DR).
Channel access shall be unslotted ALOHA subject to the regional duty-cycle limit (e.g. 1% per sub-band in EU868).

Each frame shall carry a 4-byte MIC (AES-128-CMAC with NwkSKey); the application payload shall be encrypted with AES-128 (AppSKey); the frame counter (FCnt) shall be included in the MIC and checked for replay.
MAC commands (LinkCheck, LinkADR, DutyCycle, RXParamSetup, DevStatus, NewChannel, RXTimingSetup, TxParamSetup) shall manage the link, carried in FOpts or on FPort 0.

error_response_conditions: MIC verification failure — frame discarded (integrity/authenticity check failed).
Frame-counter (FCnt) not greater than the last accepted value — frame rejected as a replay.
Payload CRC error on an uplink — frame dropped at the gateway/server.
No downlink received in RX1 or RX2 — device returns to sleep (Class A).
Join-Accept not received within the join windows — OTAA join retried with backoff.
Duty-cycle budget exhausted — transmission deferred until the sub-band is available again.
